classification.evidence: The rack's software splits into weakly-connected worlds — an off-rack nv-rms management plane, the OOB LAN rail that every BMC hangs off, the NVSwitch tray (NVOS + NMX-C/T), and an in-band compute chain (Kubernetes -> GPU Operator -> DCGM -> dcgm-exporter / Driver+CUDA -> Fabric Mgr) — and the OOB world shares no edge with the in-band world because the source calls OOB a 'separate physical Ethernet network ... distinct from every traffic-carrying fabric'.
tie_breakers: Density (E about N: 12 relations / 13 nodes) would suggest flow-chains, but the graph has four weakly-connected components and a source-named shared bus (the OOB LAN rail), so tie-breaker 2 (bus + disconnected worlds => placement-planes) decides.
Motion is not a signature here: the source never animates anything, so the case is static and no dot is drawn in any view (tie-breaker 4 does not select a family).
Identifier density is low — the content is software names and protocols, not addresses or uncertainty markers — so identity-probe-maps (tie-breaker 3) does not apply.
Bus-looks-like-a-chain check: nv-rms does look like a shallow chain into the device classes, but it is a controller client, not a bus, so it is drawn as separate API edges, never as a trunk.
classification.secondary_recipe: flow-chains habits inside the in-band world of v1 (one node per rank, corridor room reserved by label_slot, no invented side branches); the redundant-fabrics habit (parallel lanes/trunks) was deliberately NOT applied — the only bundle in the case is the OOB rail the human asked for.
